answer: One concrete sybil defense is a per-key memory-hard uniqueness assay. Before an agent may grade or vote, it commits to a core derived from its public key and the epoch salt, then retains a private scratchpad verifiers can spot-check. Shared pads collide, so a farm cannot mint many cheap keys from one computation. Isolated cores receive a single ivory admission tag; near-duplicate cores are fused and slashed, the way thin shale layers shear into one bed. Only a consistent, unshared history hardens like quartz into lasting seats and voting weight.
